_comment: Smoke set for bench/dialogue_consistency.py. Each dialogue is a list of USER turns; loom's own answer is the assistant turn from then on (autoregressive). task_type names the kind of multi-turn consistency the dialogue probes, after a published taxonomy of multi-turn abilities. The dialogues are synthetic: no dataset rows, neutral names. Numbers and constraints are chosen so a lost fact shows up as a contradiction, not as vagueness.

turns: In our PE class the sit-up standard is 28. Exceeding it is recorded as a positive number and falling short as negative. The ten results were -2, +5, -1, 0, +1, +3, 0, +8, +1, +6. What is the actual number of sit-ups each student did?
How many students met or exceeded the standard, and what percentage of the ten is that?
Who did the most and the fewest sit-ups, in actual counts?
There are three rooms. If Room 1 is occupied then Room 2 is not. If Room 2 is occupied then Room 1 is not. I checked Room 1 and it is occupied. What can you infer about Room 2?
I forgot to mention Room 3: it is occupied only if Room 2 is not. Is Room 3 occupied?
One more rule: not all rooms can be occupied. Does that change your conclusions about the three rooms?
I started at Globex in June 2022 as a data engineer. Before that I was at Acme from 2020.
Where do I work now and since when?
Correction: I actually left Globex in March 2024 and joined ClickHouse. Please update that.
Summarise my employment history in order with dates.
My team's on-call rotation is weekly and hand-off is every Tuesday at 10:00 UTC. Remember that.
When is our on-call hand-off?
Are you sure? I think it was Thursday.
So which day is the hand-off, and how long is a rotation?
We are planning the Q4 launch for the Nova connector. The deadline is 15 November and the owner is Priya.
Unrelated: what is a good way to structure a weekly one-on-one with a new report?
Back to the launch — who owns it and when is it due?
List the risks of moving our analytics database to a new region: I count four — data residency, replication lag, cost during dual-running, and DNS cutover errors.
Rephrase that in plain language for a non-technical sponsor, keeping the same four risks.
Now give them as bullet points, one line each, still the same four.
Our two services are billing-api and ledger-worker. billing-api is written in Go and deployed on Tuesdays; ledger-worker is Python and deploys daily.
Which one deploys daily, and what language is it in?
And the other one — when does it deploy?
